prompt: A rectangular prism has length $3$ in, width $4$ in, and height $5$ in. What is its **volume** in cubic inches?
hint: Volume counts the unit cubes that fill a box. Which three measurements does a rectangular prism give you to multiply?
explanation: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height, because that counts the cubes in one layer and then the number of layers.
Put in the measurements from the problem: $V = 3 \times 4 \times 5$.
Multiply the first two numbers to get the cubes in one layer: $3 \times 4 = 12$.
There are $5$ layers, so multiply again: $12 \times 5 = 60$.
The volume of the prism is $60$ cubic inches.

alternativeExplanations.title: Stack of layers method
steps: The bottom of the prism is a $3$ by $4$ rectangle, so its area is $3 \times 4 = 12$ square inches.
A layer one inch thick sitting on that base holds $12$ unit cubes.
The prism is $5$ inches tall, so it is a stack of $5$ of these layers.
Five layers of $12$ cubes make $12 \times 5 = 60$ cubes, so the volume is $60$ cubic inches.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why "cubic" inches?
steps: Multiplying $3$ in by $4$ in by $5$ in multiplies three lengths, so the unit becomes in $\times$ in $\times$ in, or in³.
Volume fills a space with depth, so it is measured in **cubic** units, not square ones.
If you packed the prism with sugar cubes that are $1$ inch on every edge, exactly $3 \times 4 \times 5 = 60$ of them would fit, so the volume is $60$ cubic inches.

hints.text: Volume counts the unit cubes that fill a box. Which three measurements does a rectangular prism give you to multiply?
Use volume equals length times width times height with these numbers: set up $3 \times 4 \times 5$ and multiply two of them first.
$3 \times 4 = 12$ and $12 \times 5 = 60$, so the volume is $60$ cubic inches.
